title: Parts of the Body
description: Name major body parts and locate simple pain or discomfort.
objectives: Name major body parts and locate simple pain or discomfort.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to name major body parts and locate simple pain or discomfort. The central language is body nouns and possessive forms. It belongs to the practical context of health & everyday problems. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: My back hurts after long trips.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the parts of the body exchange.

blocks.english: I have pain in my left shoulder.
blocks.explanation: This parts of the body model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the parts of the body exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “My back hurts after long trips.” and “I have pain in my left shoulder.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: body nouns and possessive forms.

items: Communicative goal: Name major body parts and locate simple pain or discomfort.
Core pattern: body nouns and possessive forms.
Use one clear model, add a relevant detail, and respond to the other speaker.
